title: Azure Functions Host and Worker Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:diagnostics` events with `Category="FunctionAppLogs" (level="Error" OR level="Critical")` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.5.4 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:diagnostics` traffic without `Category="FunctionAppLogs" (level="Error" OR level="Critical")`. Confirm UC-4.5.4 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:diagnostics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" Category="FunctionAppLogs" (level="Error" OR level="Critical")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.4_azure_functions_host_and_4"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.5.4 — Azure Functions Host and Worker Health: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:diagnostics` for search criteria `Category="FunctionAppLogs" (level="Error" OR level="Critical")` and returns actor, resource, and region context for availability review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Azure Functions Host and Worker Health' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.5.4 drives high-priority availability alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Stream Function App diagnostics (FunctionAppLogs) to Event Hub and ingest with the Microsoft Cloud Services add-on. Normalize `resourceName` (app name) and severity. Optionally join with `mscs:azure:metrics` for `Http5xx` or `FunctionExecutionCount` drops. Alert on sustained host-level errors or absence of successful executions.
visualization: Timeline (errors by app), Table (resourceName, message pattern, count), Status indicator (healthy/degraded per Function App).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:diagnostics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.5.16.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Stream Function App diagnostics (FunctionAppLogs) to Event Hub and ingest with the Microsoft Cloud Services add-on. Normalize `resourceName` (app name) and severity. Optionally join with `mscs:azure:metrics` for `Http5xx` or `FunctionExecutionCount` drops. Alert on sustained host-level errors or absence of successful executions.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" Category="FunctionAppLogs" (level="Error" OR level="Critical")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.4_azure_functions_host_and_4"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:diagnostics` in `index=azure` to detect azure functions host and worker health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_5_4_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Timeline (errors by app), Table (resourceName, message pattern, count), Status indicator (healthy/degraded per Function App)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure functions host and worker health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
